- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 3–5% in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is falling, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to avoid under-shoot.
- Model frequently overcorrects after strong mean-reversion periods — if price recently moved sharply from high to low, forecast should be slightly below recent low to avoid “reversion overshoot.”
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33–0.84), model often fails to capture short-term sentiment momentum — use sentiment average over last 3 days as a smoothing filter for correction.
